newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks extend losses, seen little changed.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks extend losses, seen little changed.

text.p: Croatian stocks extended their losses on Thursday in diversified activity, but traders foresaw few and very slight price changes possibly till after Easter.
"I don't expect big changes tomorrow or next week," said Velimir Zelimorski of brokerage Fima and added:
"Prices have been known to fall on Friday as dealers accept just any price. I sometimes call it the 'day of the desperate'."

For now, buyers seemed to focus on a few selected issues before committing more funds, and market watchers pointed to a lack of stronger impetus needed to reverse the downward trend of the past few weeks.
"Investors, particularly foreigners are holding back," said Davor Relja, analyst at Faktor brokerage in the port town of Split.
"But some shares have hit rock bottom; they are bound to recover slightly maybe even next week," he added.
Among those given a 'buy' recommendation at the moment is food stock Podravka, losing two kuna to 310 on Thursday with 3,007 shares sold.
Volume almost doubled to 13,577 units and turnover rose to 7.8 from 4.0 million kuna as 15 issues traded. Six of them fell, only three rose and six closed flat.
The most active stock was Pliva pharmaceuticals, adding one kuna to close at 421 on volume of 5,243 shares.
"Pliva seems to be consolidating around 420 kuna, but that cannot be a realistic price for it," said Zelimorski.
Relja said the situation might change after Pliva releases its 1996 profit report, expected toward the end of the month:
"Its results are said to be good, we have to wait and see."

Investors in another blue chip, Zagrebacka Banka, also seemed to lose patience waiting for the bank's credit rating. Its ordinary shares ended the day flat at 1,825 kuna on volume of 1,919 units, after dipping to 1,800 kuna earlier.
Top gainer Varazdinska Banka first issue rose 50 percent to 42,000 kuna but only one share was traded.
The biggest loser was textile firm Varteks, falling eight kuna or 9.4 percent to 77 kuna on volume of 1,100 units.
Varteks is hoped to be majority privatised soon to help the company renew its licence for making Levi's jeans. A 31-percent stake in it was included in the mass voucher scheme last week.

Hoteliers Istraturist and Suncani Hvar also sank in expectation of Easter holidays, thought to be a first indication of the foreign bookings for this summer. But Istrian Laguna gained 21 kuna to 1,440 and Jadranturist was flat.
"All their prospects will probably be clearer after Easter," Relja said.
